result.name: Each entity the shipment reaches is to prove, and nothing else
A shipment that reaches no entity has nothing to migrate

fields.context: The data a product kept outside the graph was described twice: a TypeScript interface, and a decision naming its tables and columns, or the names of its preferences; the code joined the two by texts and casts, read what was stored by a rule written by hand, and nothing saw a change of shape before stored data broke. The kinds of the language could not say it: a decision holds a value but knows no version deployed, and a status that says every version deployed reads into this one, nobody could compute (A5).
fields.consequences: A project that imports the library writes entities: their fields, each with how it is stored, their key. Wired, an entity gives its model: the type of a value (EntityOf), the names of its fields as values, the version of its description and the migration from each version deployed, computed from what each deployment kept; what a migration cannot decide blocks, for the owner to decide in its changes. A document is read migrated and checked, or not at all. The kind is the library's (src/kinds), with its laws played by every build, its words in a catalog, and the example of examples/kept.

rejected.Composing the kinds of the language: a decision for the shape, functions for the migrations, written by hand: the description twice again, and no status for what deployments kept
rejected.Migrations written by hand, version afte: what a difference between two descriptions computes, a person would write again, and forget
rejected.The kind in the language itself: storing data is the concern of the products that keep some (A5): a library they import

postgres.create: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS books (title TEXT PRIMARY KEY, pages DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL, shelf TEXT NOT NULL, lent INTEGER)
postgres.find: SELECT title, pages, shelf, lent FROM books WHERE title = $1
postgres.update: UPDATE books SET pages = $1 WHERE title = $2
postgres.add: ALTER TABLE books ADD COLUMN lent INTEGER
postgres.exists: SELECT table_name FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_name = $1

result.name: A document written is read back as it was, with the version of its description
What was stored before versions were kept is read as the first version deployed
A document of a version deployed is migrated: a field renamed moves, one dropped goes
A document that does not keep its description is nothing: a number written as a text, a word of no vocabulary
A document of a version nothing migrates from is nothing

fields.context: The library's documents are read and written as a product's would be, the device in memory.

result.name: PostgreSQL's statements name their parameters by position, type a number as double precision, and ask the information schema whether a table exists
A table of a version deployed is migrated the first time it is used: a column renamed (its key), one dropped, one added; its rows read as the description is now, and the version kept is this one
A record inserted is found by its key, as it was; the table counts it
A record updated takes its new values, and keeps the others
A transaction that fails writes nothing
A row that does not keep its description is nothing

fields.context: Records are written, migrated and read by SQLite itself, as a product's would be, and nothing is left behind.
